transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because I started eating cleaner for the lieutenant track, but it’s gotten pretty restrictive. Some days, even on shift, I’ll just have black coffee, a protein shake, and a small dinner, even though I know I’ve burned way more than that.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

Yeah. If the scale goes up even a pound—like after a big meal at the station or just drinking more water—I get this tight, panicky feeling. Like I’ve messed up and people are going to see me as soft or out of control.
Are you currently at a low body weight for your height?

Yeah. My gear and station clothes are hanging a lot looser, and the fitness review flagged my weight as too low for my build. But honestly, part of me still feels like I could stand to trim down a little more.
Do you ever have episodes where you eat an unusually large amount of food in a short period of time and feel unable to stop?
No, I don’t think so. I’m usually more focused on keeping what I eat controlled than eating a lot at once.
Have you ever made yourself vomit after eating?
I’m not sure what you mean exactly. I haven’t really thought about that.
After eating, have you ever made yourself throw up to try to prevent weight gain?
I haven’t really noticed myself doing that. I’m not sure—do you mean on purpose, right after eating?
Have you ever made yourself throw up on purpose after eating?
I’m not sure. I don’t really know if I’ve done that on purpose after eating.
Have you ever used laxatives or diuretics to keep from gaining weight?
I don’t think so. I’m not really sure what counts as those, but I haven’t noticed myself using anything like that to avoid gaining weight.
Do you deliberately try to keep your weight below what is healthy for you?
Yeah, I guess I do. My gear and station clothes are hanging looser, and the fitness review said my weight was too low for my build, but part of me still thinks I should trim down a little more.
When you look in the mirror, do you see yourself as overweight?

I don’t exactly see myself as overweight, but I do focus on whether my waist and face look sharp enough. If they don’t, especially before work, it can make me feel less confident and less command-ready that day.
Do you ever exercise specifically to burn off calories or prevent weight gain after eating?
I’m not sure. I exercise for work and to stay fit, but I haven’t really thought of it as trying to burn off something I ate.
Do you ever intentionally go for long periods without eating to keep yourself from gaining weight?

Yeah. It started as trying to eat cleaner for the lieutenant track, but now I’ll go most of a shift with just black coffee and a protein shake, then have a small dinner. Even when I know I’ve burned a lot that day, I still keep it that way so I don’t gain weight.
Have you ever made yourself vomit on purpose to keep from gaining weight?
No, I haven’t done that.
Have you ever used laxatives or water pills on purpose to keep from gaining weight?
No, I haven’t used anything like that.
Have you had times when you ate a very large amount of food within a short period and felt unable to stop?
I’m not sure what counts as a very large amount. I don’t think I’ve had times where I felt like I couldn’t stop eating.
